docRequirement: skills.md:547 binds `context: fork` to isolation: "Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent. It won't have access to your conversation history." Three frontmatter fields depend on it and are specified in the same reference table: `agent` (:270) "Which subagent type to use when `context: fork` is set"; `background` (:271) "Only applies with `context: fork`. Set to `false` to wait for the forked subagent's result in the turn that invoked the skill, instead of running it in the background. Default: `true`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later"; and independently `hooks` (:272) "Hooks scoped to this skill's lifecycle" and `shell` (:274) "Shell to use for !`command` and ```! blocks in this skill. Accepts `bash` (default) or `powershell`". The :570 table further binds a forked skill's system prompt to the agent type and its task to the SKILL.md content.
current: All four keys are parsed by nothing. `SkillMetadataSchema` is `.passthrough()` and declares none of them (packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.ts:268-286); `DOCUMENTED_SKILL_FIELDS` (validation.ts:212-221) omits them; `IGNORED_SKILL_FIELDS` (validation.ts:246-251) lists all four with reasons, and its only consumer is validation.ts:352-359, which emits an author-facing WARNING ("'<key>' is a documented field this runtime does not implement — it will be ignored"). Pinned by packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.test.ts:60-72. The runtime read of a SKILL.md is `materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:831-902): it takes `allowed-tools`/`tools` (:869), `model` (:870), `agent` (:871), `effort` (:850) and `disallowed-tools` (:877-881) into `restrictions` and reads no `context`, `background`, `hooks` or `shell`. `RuntimeSkillHandle` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:69-109) carries no fork field either. The invocation body then goes INLINE into the live conversation: `formatPinnedSkillInstructions` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2395-2399) joins `formatRuntimeSkillInvocation` output (runtime-skill-content.ts:1075-1078) and it is injected on the model path at base-agent.ts:2676-2679 ("You invoked the skill above. Follow its instructions and continue the task.") and on the user path at base-agent.ts:2794 — same turn, same history, same context budget. The neighbouring `agent` field IS honoured but with different meaning: `applySkillInvocationGrant` (base-agent.ts:2540-2564) turns it into a per-turn agent CEILING via `setSkillInvocationAgentCeiling` (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prerequisite-manager.ts:212-214) and throws `Invoked skill agent unavailable` at :2558 — never a spawn target. The repo's own `fork` is the opposite construct: `FORK_AGENT_NAME`/`FORK_AGENT_DEFINITION` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:208-232) is described as "a subagent that inherits the full message history, system prompt, tools and model of this session" (:221), reached by `/subtask` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6295-6310 `requestSubtaskFork`) and admitted at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10833-10839; no skill frontmatter routes into it. For `shell`, the in-file reason ("inline shell blocks always run under bash") overstates what exists: `expandRuntimeSkillBody` (runtime-skill-content.ts:629-699) performs variable and `$ARGUMENTS` substitution only, with no `` !`command` `` pass at all, and the plugin importer treats that syntax as an unsupported deferral in Claude prompt commands (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:653-657, :741-749); `grep -a disableSkillShellExecution` over packages/ and apps/ returns nothing. For `hooks`, frontmatter hook declarations in plugin-supplied skills and agents are refused out loud with a deferral (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:410-436 `reportFrontmatterHookDeclarations`), but no per-skill hook scope exists. Plugin-imported skills project only description, `disableModelInvocation`, `userInvocable`, `allowedTools` and `paths` (format-adapters.ts:517-552 `applyPluginSkillFrontmatter`), so a plugin skill's `context: fork` is dropped silently at import with no deferred row.
divergence: Not a key-name or value mismatch — the field names and accepted values match the page exactly; there is simply no consumer. A skill declaring `context: fork` runs INLINE in the main conversation with full history, instead of as an isolated subagent whose prompt is the SKILL.md content, and its result never arrives as a separate background completion. `background` is inert because its governing field is; `agent` is honoured but re-purposed as a per-turn agent ceiling rather than skills.md:270's fork target; `hooks` has no per-component lifecycle scope; `shell` has no interpreter to select because inline `` !`command` `` execution does not exist in skill bodies at all (so validation.ts:250's stated reason is itself inaccurate). The delta is a missing isolation guarantee, not an inverted one: dropping `context` yields exactly the behaviour a fieldless skill gets.

change.what: Read `frontmatter.context` (accept only the literal `fork`) and `frontmatter.background` (LooseBoolean, default true) alongside the existing reads at :869-:881, and pin them onto the record as a NEW optional `fork?: { agent?: string; background: boolean }` — deliberately separate from `restrictions.agent`, which stays the turn ceiling. Append the key LAST in `frozenUnsignedRecord` and in the snapshot validator, exactly as the `disallowedTools` rollout did (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-inert-unit-e.md), so `computeSkillInvocationDigest` produces the identical JSON key set for a record without it.

Add `context?: 'fork'` and `background?: boolean` beside `disableModelInvocation`/`userInvocable`/`allowedTools` (:82-:96) so the listing and `/slug` registration can show that a skill forks before it is invoked; populate them in the resolver that already pins `skillDisableModelInvocation` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1007-1009).

Split the invocation set on `fork`. A forked invocation must NOT enter `activeSkillInvocations`, must NOT reach `formatPinnedSkillInstructions` (:2395) and must NOT go through `applySkillInvocationGrant` (:2540) — its grants belong to the child. Instead dispatch it: prompt = the already-expanded `invocation.body`, agent type = `restrictions.agent` (falling back to the general agent, never to `fork`, whose whole meaning is history inheritance), history = none. With `background: false` await the child result in the invoking turn; otherwise return immediately and deliver the result as a later message.

Add a sibling start RPC for a skill fork carrying { agent, prompt, background } — do not overload `subtask_start`, whose contract is the history-inheriting `/subtask` fork and whose promise deliberately resolves at ADMISSION (:6289-:6293). The `background: false` variant needs a result-carrying reply, which the current admission-only shape cannot express.

Accept the new spawn kind. Most of the work already exists here: :11018-:11021 already composes a child prompt from `formatRuntimeSkillInvocation` output for the preload-skills-into-subagents direction, and :10833-:10839 already branches on fork requests. Add the inverse case — prompt IS the skill body, agent comes from the skill's `agent`, no parent history — reusing the existing tool narrowing (:10993-:11016) and admission evaluation. If the doc's narrower background tool set (:557) is adopted, apply it only on the background branch.

Move `context` and `background` up to the honoured list once they are read — the rule the file already states at :244. Independently, and as a one-line fix that stands alone: correct the `shell` reason at :250, which claims "inline shell blocks always run under bash" when no inline shell block runs at all; say that skill bodies perform no `` !`command` `` execution. Leave `hooks` where it is.

blastRadius: Crosses a PERSISTENCE boundary and a WIRE boundary, both AGENTS.md risk triggers. Persistence: `SkillInvocationRecord` is digest-signed and reattached across resume (`computeSkillInvocationDigest`, `assertSkillInvocationBudget`, `MAX_SKILL_INVOCATION_BYTES` in runtime-skill-content.ts:14, and the snapshot validator), and its handles are dereferenced later by packages/shared/src/capabilities/skill-resource-resolver.ts:86-143, which compares `invocation.generation` and `sourceDigest` — any new key must be appended last or every pre-existing record's digest changes. Wire: host→Pi subprocess, `subtask_start`/`subtask_start_result` (pi-agent.ts:2272, :6304) plus the `runtime-agent-*` child admission contract in SessionManager.ts. Other readers of the invocation set: base-agent.ts:2398 (turn text), SessionManager.ts:11021 (child prompt preload), prerequisite-manager.ts:201-214 (tool and agent ceilings), and `narrowRuntimeSkillTools`/`collectSkillDisallowedTools` (runtime-skill-content.ts:1003, :1042). Backend-wide, not Pi-only: claude-agent.ts:1627 records that skills are handled by `BaseAgent.chat()`, so every backend takes the same inline path. Imported-plugin path: packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters.ts:517 `applyPluginSkillFrontmatter` must learn the field or plugin skills keep losing it silently; the parallel refusal precedent is `reportFrontmatterHookDeclarations` at :436. Tests to update: packages/session-tools-core/src/validation.test.ts:60-72, packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/runtime-skill-content.test.ts (formatting and digest cases at :204, :451, :484, :512), and the orchestrator's packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/subagent-tool.test.ts and fork-mode.test.ts if the spawn path is reused.
userImpact: Observable, and worst for installed plugins. A user runs a skill written for Claude Code with `context: fork` — say a research or PR-summary skill whose whole point is a throwaway context — and instead of a background subagent returning a summary, the entire SKILL.md is spliced into the live conversation and executed there: full history visible to the task (the opposite of what the skill's prompt assumes), the main context window consumed by the skill's own work, no separate background completion message, and no way to keep working while it runs. Nothing at invocation time says so. The author-facing warning added by 55b711ce is reachable only through an explicit `skill_validate` call (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/skill-validate.ts:116-129) or the config-doctor aggregate (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:487); the write-time gate at packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:509-517 acts on `!validationResult.valid` only, so warnings are dropped when a SKILL.md is written through a tool. And a Claude PLUGIN whose skill sets `context: fork` imports as fully supported — `applyPluginSkillFrontmatter` (format-adapters.ts:517-552) never looks at the key, so unlike a frontmatter `hooks` block there is no deferred row in Sources and no diagnostic anywhere. `background` and `shell` produce no separate symptom beyond this. One direction where we are safer, not worse: skills.md:559 warns that a backgrounded fork's edits escape `/rewind`; ours run inside the session and stay checkpointed.
